# Cully 0.15.0

This release is about showing whether Cully is worth its tokens, and about making the advisor better at saving them.

- **See what Cully did for you.** The panel's Cully column now shows impact for the terminal session: memory used, analyses avoided, loops caught and net tokens, with one MCP health line. The new `cully impact [--days N] [--json] [--log]` reports the same over time from a local ledger of counts and token estimates (no content). A memory saving is claimed only when `cully savings` has enough sessions to compare; otherwise the report says it is not claimed, and an empty ledger says nothing was recorded.
- **Measure the cost honestly.** `cully savings` reads local Claude Code transcripts and reports the tokens Cully's calls inject, tool schemas and arguments, plus a confidence-labelled estimate of exploration avoided when a lookup returned prior work. On the maintainer's machine it found Cully costing more than it saved, mostly because saved records were echoed back into the agent's context.
- **Smaller write replies.** MCP `cully_log` and `cully_update` now return a compact acknowledgement (id, section, project, session references, timestamps) instead of the saved record. The native agent session ID is kept so a note can still resume its conversation. Clients that read the saved text from a write reply should call `cully_get`.
- **Advisor finds token waste.** The advisor now sees oversized tool results, whole-file reads, noisy Bash output and Cully's own result tokens. When the waste is significant it suggests the single most important fix, with the numbers, and may ask its research step to look for a published tool. It stays quiet otherwise.
- **Test the advisor on past sessions.** `cully advisor-eval` replays transcripts at 30, 60 and 90 percent through the same signals and judges the advice in hindsight; `--live N` also runs the real advisor, memory recall and web research. It reads personal-project transcripts by default and keeps no transcript text. On 20 real sessions only 2 triggered advice, so the precision and recall figures are too thin to tune on; collect more sessions before changing thresholds.
- **A divider you can see and grab.** The panel's resize bar is now a heavy tinted bar with a grip chip, brighter under the pointer and solid while dragging, and asks the terminal for a vertical-resize pointer where supported.
- **Mobile Self gets a dated Today briefing** with a last-24-hours view, a sampled seven-day review, projects, recorded learnings and explicit continuation drafts. Android and iOS versions are 0.15.0.
- **Tavric Labs.** Repository, installer, SDK and container references moved to the `tavric-labs` organization; images publish under `ghcr.io/tavric-labs`. Existing Go module imports are unchanged. The docs and website deployments need their VM controller moved to the new image namespace before they deploy again (see `deploy/website.md`).
- **Optional T3 Code support** as a multi-agent surface (`docs/t3code.md`).

See `docs/token-efficiency-plan.md` for the measured baseline and the work still planned.

The mobile Android APK, when attached, is a development-signed preview as in 0.14.0; the iOS app is source-only. Models, tokens and signing keys are not included.
